title: Deployment and modern trends
subtitle: Getting code from a laptop to users, repeatably and safely.

env.title: Environments
env.body: Code moves through environments: development (your machine), staging (a production-like copy for final checks), production (real users). Configuration (URLs, secrets) comes from environment variables, never committed to the repository — the same build runs everywhere.

ci.title: CI/CD pipeline
ci.body: Every push triggers: install → lint → test → build → deploy to staging → (approval) → deploy to production. A failing stage stops the line. Automated pipelines make releases boring.

cont.title: Containers
cont.body: A container (Docker) packages an app with its dependencies, so “works on my machine” means works everywhere. An image is the recipe; a container is a running instance. Kubernetes schedules, scales and heals containers across machines.

rel.title: Safe release strategies
rel.body: Blue–green: run old (blue) and new (green) side by side, switch traffic, switch back if broken. Canary: send 5 % of traffic to the new version first. Feature flags ship code turned off. Always have a fast rollback.
rel.steps: A bug affects 2 % of requests. A 5 % canary sees it on: 0.05 × 0.02 = 0.1 % of all traffic, instead of 2 %.

perf.title: Performance and caching
perf.body: Minify and compress (gzip/brotli), cache static files with long max-age and hashed names, serve from a CDN near the user, lazy-load images, avoid render-blocking scripts. Measure with Core Web Vitals: LCP (loading), INP (responsiveness), CLS (layout stability).

trend.title: Modern trends
trend.body: Serverless functions (pay per call), edge computing, server-side rendering with hydration, Progressive Web Apps (installable, offline), WebAssembly for near-native speed, WebSockets/SSE for real-time updates, and AI-assisted development. Pick the simplest architecture that meets the need.
